facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: one audited annual report, three unaudited interim reports and three releases cover FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 with prior-year comparatives. Together they support a financial foundation, a debt and lease map, and the merger narrative up to October 27, 2026. - Strongest contrary evidence: the pending acquisition can change ownership and leverage. The Q3 10-Q lists risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction (page:57) and the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all. The supplied text does not say how the existing CEI debt or the CVA facilities are treated at closing. - Source risk mechanism: lease payments to VICI and GLPI run through Long-term financing obligations and interest expense, not through the debt table, and Adjusted EBITDA excludes the expense associated with certain of our leases (Q3 release page:3). A consumer reading only total debt or Adjusted EBITDA would understate fixed claims and overstate coverage. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must carry the lease obligations and the lease cash interest alongside debt. - Second mechanism: the covenant definitions govern headroom, and the company states that its Adjusted EBITDA definition may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt or lease agreements (Q3 10-Q page:49). Consequence: CP-2 can report printed levels and the compliance statement but cannot verify headroom. - What cannot proceed: merger financing analysis, post-closing capital structure, covenant headroom on agreement definitions, guarantor-level and restricted-group analysis, and any event after October 27, 2026. - Next evidence action: supply the Merger Agreement (Form 8-K filed May 28, 2026, Exhibit 2.1), the merger proxy statement filed August 26, 2026, any financing commitment papers, the CEI Credit Agreement and indentures, and the VICI and GLPI lease agreements; and any filing dated October 28, 2026 to November 5, 2026.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base supports a debt-only view and a lease-inclusive view, and the two give very different pictures. On the company's own measures, debt is 11,659 at Q3 2026 (face value), net debt is 10,795, and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 3,573, giving 3.26x and 3.02x. But Adjusted EBITDA is stated before the rent on the VICI and GLPI leases, which the company accounts for as financing obligations of 13,188 outside debt. Adding those obligations lifts leverage to 6.95x, and adding the roughly 1,371 of rent cash interest to the 741 of cash interest on debt gives cash interest cover of 1.69x. Both views use the same company Adjusted EBITDA, so neither is a covenant ratio. Earnings are drifting lower (Adjusted EBITDA 2,672 for 9M 2026 against 2,723 for 9M 2025, with Las Vegas down and Regional and Digital up) and net loss attributable to Caesars widened to (283) from (252). Liquidity is adequate in the near term and nothing in the debt table matures before 2028 beyond amortisation. The pending acquisition adds uncertainty about the debt, but the supplied sources do not say how existing debt is treated.

facts.label: Leases and other claims outside debt
facts.text: - Financing obligations: Long-term financing obligations were 13,188 at September 30, 2026, 13,157 at June 30, 2026, 13,126 at March 31, 2026 and 13,096 at December 31, 2025 (balance sheets, page:2). They arise from failed sale-leasebacks with VICI and GLPI. The 10-K splits them at December 31, 2025 as GLPI Leases 1,284 and VICI Leases 11,705 (10-K page:117), which total 12,989; the remaining 107 of the 13,096 balance is not itemised in the text read. The 10-Qs give no split. - Why the balance grows: cash payments are less than the interest expense recognized, which causes the failed-sale leaseback obligation to increase during the initial years of the lease term (10-K page:118). The increase from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 is 92 (calculated). - Rent cash: cash interest paid for rent was 1,349 in FY2025 and 1,030 for GLPI and VICI in 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). Management estimates approximately $345 million of lease payments to VICI and GLPI for the remainder of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:51) and approximately $1.4 billion for 2026 (10-K page:80). - Contractual terms: VICI leases have a 15-year initial term with four five-year renewals, CPI escalators with a 2% floor and a net revenue variable element; the next variable adjustment year begins in November 2027 (10-K page:116; Q3 10-Q page:51). The GLPI Master Lease runs through September 2038 with escalators (10-K page:117). The lease covenants require a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1 for the GLPI Leases (Q3 10-Q page:52). - Operating and finance leases: operating lease liability 742 and finance lease liabilities 147 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:115 and page:116). The 10-Qs show no update beyond 203 of right-of-use assets obtained in exchange for lease liabilities in 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5); the filing does not state which lease it relates to. Separately, the Caesars Windsor lease has annual minimum rent of about 19 (Q3 10-Q page:10). - Other commitments: sports sponsorship obligations 309 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15); self-insurance liability 244 (page:15). Defined-benefit plans are small: the Tropicana Atlantic City plan had assets of 33 and obligations of 22, and the Scioto Downs plan about 1 each (10-K page:140). Multi-employer pension plan participation exists (10-K page:141); withdrawal liability amounts were not found. No factoring or supply-chain finance programme was found in the pack. - Litigation and the data incident: the 10-K states the Data Incident has not had a material impact (10-K page:121); Q3 2026 litigation liabilities are not material (Q3 10-Q page:15). Merger-related suits have been threatened or filed (Q3 10-Q page:65), with no amount.

facts.label: Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication
facts.text: - Earnings: Adjusted EBITDA for 9M 2026 is 2,672 against 2,723, with Las Vegas 1,179 against 1,281 and Regional 1,447 against 1,385 (Q3 10-Q page:31 to page:32). The Las Vegas decline is attributed to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation (Q3 10-Q page:46). Credit implication: the large Las Vegas segment, which carries the VICI Las Vegas lease, is the weak spot, and Regional growth includes the Windsor consolidation. - Fixed charges: Adjusted EBITDA is before lease rent, so the lease cash interest of about 1,371 is a charge ahead of any debt service. Cash interest on debt is 741 and net loss attributable to Caesars is (533) over the last twelve months; interest expense, net of 2,287 exceeds operating income of 1,801 over the same period, and it includes lease interest. Credit implication: cover on all fixed charges is thin even though debt-only leverage looks moderate. - Cash generation: 9M 2026 operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment is 435 against 350, helped by lower capital expenditure (507 against 648) rather than higher operating cash (942 against 998). Credit implication: free cash flow depends on capital expenditure discipline; the 4.99% ratio to debt is low for the leverage. - Liquidity and maturities: liquidity on the company basis is 2,947 including cash of 864, with the revolver undrawn. Debt maturing before 2029 is small (28 in remaining 2026, 114 in 2027, 646 in 2028), then 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030. Credit implication: refinancing risk concentrates in 2029 and 2030, and the revolver and Term Loan A mature January 31, 2028, about fifteen months after the as-of date. - Quality of the evidence: the quarterly statements are unaudited. The FY2025 statements are audited: the auditor states they present fairly, in all material respects the financial position and results (10-K page:96), in a report dated February 17, 2026 (10-K page:98). Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and the cash-interest lines are management or supplemental presentations; the 10-K labels Adjusted EBITDA as unaudited (10-K page:77).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit story is a large, lease-heavy casino operator with a diversified but physically concentrated revenue base, entering a change of control on terms the sources describe only in part. Regional properties and Las Vegas supply about 85% of net revenues, Caesars Digital is the growing third leg, and the VICI and GLPI real estate leases make the company a tenant at 25 of the 47 casinos it owns or leases. Ownership today is public, with about 273 holders of record, no sponsor named in the context and no dividend history. The pending merger converts each share into cash of $31.00 plus a ticking fee after June 26, 2027, was approved by stockholders on September 22, 2026, and remains subject to antitrust and gaming approvals with an outside date that can run to November 27, 2027. For creditors, the open questions are who finances the purchase, whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, and whether leverage rises; the sources state that financing risk exists but give no terms. Until the Merger Agreement, proxy statement and financing papers are supplied, the transaction can be described but not assessed for debt effects.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction is a pending cash acquisition of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. On May 27, 2026 the company, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, Empire Merger Sub, Inc., Landry's Fertitta, LLC (for Section 9.14 of the agreement only) and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. (for Section 9.14(j) only) signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which Merger Sub merges into the company and the company survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases state that the agreement is with Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. and that it was announced on May 28, 2026 (Q3 release page:4). The two names are logged below as an unresolved conflict. Each share other than excluded, parent rollover and dissenting shares converts into $31.00 in cash plus, if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day from the first day of the following month; parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, and the sources do not disclose a rollover percentage (Q3 10-Q page:7). Restricted stock units are cancelled for cash at the same consideration (Q3 10-Q page:7).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The status is stockholder-approved and awaiting regulatory conditions. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and the proposals were approved at a special meeting on September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Closing remains conditioned on expiry or termination of the HSR Act waiting period and receipt of certain gaming regulatory approvals; the filings do not say which approvals have been received (Q3 10-Q page:8 and page:62). The initial end date is May 27, 2027, extended automatically to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only those regulatory conditions remain open (Q3 10-Q page:8). A termination fee of $200 million is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a reverse termination fee of $450 million by Fertitta Gaming in others, including antitrust or gaming law prohibitions or the end date occurring with only regulatory conditions open (Q3 10-Q page:9). A no-shop has applied since July 11, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:8). On completion the common stock is delisted from NASDAQ and deregistered, which ends the public filings that this credit view relies on (Q3 10-Q page:10).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. is a liquid but lease-burdened credit: debt-only leverage of 3.26x looks moderate, yet fixed-charge cover is thin and the change of control leaves the debt outlook open. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,947 million, an undrawn revolver and a first notes maturity only in 2029. The weakest point is fixed charges: USD 13,188 million of lease financing obligations sit outside debt, lifting leverage to 6.95x and holding cash interest cover to 1.69x while Adjusted EBITDA slipped to USD 2,672 million for nine months 2026. What decides the outcome is how the pending acquisition is financed and whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, which the supplied sources do not say.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, liquidity is adequate. Caesars Entertainment, Inc. held USD 864 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,083 million of revolver availability on the company basis at September 30, 2026, together USD 2,947 million, and the CEI revolver was undrawn after USD 160 million was drawn at December 31, 2025 [CP-1]. No notes mature before 2029. Debt falling due is USD 28 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 114 million in 2027 and USD 646 million in 2028, which is mostly the CEI Term Loan A of USD 609 million; the CEI revolver and that term loan both mature on January 31, 2028. Nothing matures within twelve months of the as-of date beyond scheduled amortisation, so the 2028 date becomes a current-year issue from early 2027 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

No notes mature before 2029. Debt falling due is USD 28 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 114 million in 2027 and USD 646 million in 2028, which is mostly the CEI Term Loan A of USD 609 million; the CEI revolver and that term loan both mature on January 31, 2028. Nothing matures within twelve months of the as-of date beyond scheduled amortisation, so the 2028 date becomes a current-year issue from early 2027 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the lease structure is the main fixed claim. Long-term financing obligations to VICI and GLPI of USD 13,188 million sit outside the USD 11,659 million of debt, and the lease payment schedule at December 31, 2025 shows USD 1,392 million in 2027, USD 1,424 million in 2028 and USD 1,446 million in 2029 [CP-1; annual report]. Lease cash interest of about USD 1,371 million over the last twelve months compares with USD 741 million of cash interest on debt. Adjusted EBITDA excludes this rent, so total debt plus financing obligations over Adjusted EBITDA is 6.95x against 3.26x for debt alone, and Adjusted EBITDA over all cash interest is 1.69x. Adjusted EBITDA less purchases of property and equipment of USD 664 million gives USD 2,909 million against USD 2,112 million of cash interest, or 1.38x (calculated). Net loss attributable to Caesars was USD 533 million over the last twelve months.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, leverage is flat to slightly better on debt and slightly worse once leases are counted. Debt-only leverage moved from 3.29x at FY2025 to 3.26x at Q3 2026 as debt fell by USD 246 million, while the lease-inclusive ratio moved from 6.90x to 6.95x because the financing obligation grew by USD 92 million and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 3,624 million to USD 3,573 million [CP-1]. The company explains that in the early years of these leases cash payments are below the interest expense recognised, so the obligation increases.

facts.text: Fourth, earnings are mixed by segment. Las Vegas Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,179 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,281 million, attributed by the company to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation, while Regional rose to USD 1,447 million from USD 1,385 million, helped by the Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026, and Caesars Digital rose to USD 181 million from USD 151 million [CP-1; CP-1A]. Las Vegas carries the highest segment margin, so its softness weighs more than its revenue share of 35.3% suggests (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and no near-term maturity wall: USD 2,947 million of liquidity against USD 142 million of scheduled principal through 2027, with the revolver undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Diversified footprint and a growing digital segment: 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions, Regional at 50.1% and Las Vegas at 35.3% of FY2025 net revenues, and Caesars Digital Adjusted EBITDA up to USD 181 million for nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (3) Conservative capital return and debt direction: no cash dividends, no share repurchases in nine months 2026, debt down USD 246 million since FY2025 and asset sale proceeds applied to redeeming the 2027 notes (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Moderate debt-only leverage of 3.26x and debt-only cash interest cover of 4.82x (Analyst Interpretation on company Adjusted EBITDA; CP-1). (5) Stockholder approval of the merger removes one execution uncertainty (Documentary Fact; CP-1A).

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - Debt plus financing obligations: FY2025 11,905 + 13,096 = 25,001; Q3 2026 11,659 + 13,188 = 24,847; change 24,847 - 25,001 = -154 (debt -246, obligation +92). - Lease-inclusive ratio at constant FY2025 EBITDA: 24,847 / 3,624 = 6.86x. Reported ratios: 25,001 / 3,624 = 6.90x and 24,847 / 3,573 = 6.95x. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are enough to run all four selected modules on the consolidated company, each with stated limits. Nothing blocks the work. | Medium | No credit agreements, indentures, leases, merger financing terms or filings after the third-quarter report are supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Lease financing obligations sit outside the debt table, and the lease detail by landlord is only in the annual report. | Fixed lease claims are larger than the debt figure and need separate treatment. | Medium |
| The pending acquisition is described, but its financing and effect on existing debt are not supplied. | Post-closing leverage and debt treatment cannot be assessed from these sources. | Low |
| Covenant levels and compliance statements are printed, but no covenant ratio values or governing definitions are. | Headroom cannot be verified against the agreement definitions. | Low |
### Readiness view

Every selected consumer can proceed on the supplied filings, with bounded limitations; none is conditional or blocked. The 10-K and the three 10-Qs are original authority for statements, notes and covenant text, and the three earnings releases are management-prepared support. The recurring limits are that the governing debt and lease documents are not supplied, that the pending merger's financing and its effect on existing debt are not described, and that nothing dated after the October 27, 2026 filings is supplied.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 statements (page:99 to page:101 of the 10-K) and unaudited statements for the three interim periods of 2026 are located, with prior-year comparatives. Segment, Adjusted EBITDA, debt, cash-flow and supplemental cash-interest tables are present. Limit: the 10-Qs carry no lease note, so lease detail is at December 31, 2025 only. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, properties, history, the pending merger, ownership of Caesars Virginia and the asset purchases are located. Limit: the Merger Agreement, the proxy statement and any merger financing papers are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Debt tables, maturities, guarantees, covenant levels, liquidity tables and lease financing obligations are located. Limit: no executed credit agreement, indenture or lease; no printed covenant ratio values. |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source has stable page locators, so claims can be traced. Limit: the text extraction was not compared with the filed HTML or XBRL, and no source is an image or chart that was inspected. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Source register
- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated statements. Cover at page:1: `For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025`.

- Audit: page:96 holds `REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM` on the financial statements; page:98 shows the report dated `February 17, 2026` and `We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2020.` A second report on internal control is at page:154.

- Statements: balance sheet at page:99; cash and restricted-cash reconciliation at page:101; notes from page:103. Lease note at page:115 to page:117; litigation note at page:120; long-term debt note at page:121 to page:122; segment note at page:147.
- Liquidity: the cash and borrowing capacity table is at page:79; Adjusted EBITDA discussion starts at page:77. Debt service requirements are at page:122.

- Other: the data-security event the filing defines as the `Data Incident` is described at page:39. The exhibit list names indentures and the VICI and GLPI lease amendments as `Previously filed`; their texts are not in the pack.
- Units: dollars in millions (balance sheet header at page:99). USD.
- Perimeter: consolidated Caesars Entertainment, Inc. and subsidiaries, including noncontrolling interests.
- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited. Cover at page:1: `For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026`; signed `Date: April 28, 2026` (page:50).
- Statements from page:2; debt note at page:11; covenant text at page:16; cash and borrowing capacity at page:41.
- The filing contains no mention of the pending merger (no occurrence of the word merger or of Fertitta). It was filed before the Merger Agreement.
- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited. Cover at page:1: `For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026`; signed `Date: July 28, 2026` (page:66).
- Statements from page:2; Note 1 with the first description of the merger at page:6 to page:8; debt note at page:15; covenant text at page:20; liquidity at page:50.

- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited; the latest filing in the pack. Cover at page:1: `For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026`; signed `Date: October 27, 2026` (page:66).

- Statements: balance sheet page:2; statements of operations page:2 to page:3; cash flows page:4 to page:5 with supplemental cash interest at page:5. Note 1 (merger, asset purchases) at page:6 to page:10. Note 5 (commitments) at page:15. Note 6 (debt, maturities, covenants, guarantees) at page:15 to page:21. Segment note at page:30 to page:34.
- MD&A: results from page:41; Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation at page:49 to page:50; liquidity at page:50 to page:53; market risk at page:54.
- Part II: risk factors on the merger at page:60 to page:65; exhibits at page:66, including the Merger Agreement as `Previously filed on Form 8-K filed on May 28, 2026.`
- Units: `(In millions)` throughout. USD. Statements are unaudited interim.
#### Earnings releases (three Exhibit 99.1 files)

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1, management-prepared and unaudited. They give attributed management figures and non-GAAP measures; they do not override the filings.

- Q3 release (`EX-99.1_2026-10-27_ex991-2026q3ceiearningsrel.htm.jsonl`): dated `October 27, 2026` (page:1). Segment tables on page:1; balance sheet, net debt and liquidity on page:2; non-GAAP definition on page:3; statements of operations and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation on page:5 to page:6.
- Q2 release (`EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-2026q2ceiearningsrel.htm.jsonl`): net debt table on page:2; merger and no-call statement on page:3.
- Q1 release (`EX-99.1_2026-04-28_ex991-2026q1ceiearningsrel.htm.jsonl`): net debt table on page:2. It does not mention the merger.

- Net debt is a company non-GAAP measure: the Q3 release defines it as `Net debt is equal to total outstanding indebtedness less cash and cash equivalents.` Each release repeats the 10-Q statement of operations for its period, so a release is not independent corroboration of that 10-Q.
### Information-availability boundary
- Every source is dated on or before the cutoff. The latest are the Q3 10-Q and Q3 release, both dated October 27, 2026.
- Between October 27, 2026 and the as-of date 2026-11-05, nothing is supplied. Events in that window, for example regulatory approvals or merger financing, are Not supplied, not absent.
- Q3 10-Q page:1 gives the share count as of October 22, 2026, which is inside the supplied period.

- The Q3 10-Q (page:7) reports that stockholders approved the merger proposals on September 22, 2026, and gives May 27, 2027 as the initial end date, with extensions to August 27, 2027 and November 27, 2027 (page:8). These future dates are contract terms, not events.
### Identity and perimeter

- Registrant and reporting entity: Caesars Entertainment, Inc., a Delaware corporation, NASDAQ symbol CZR, Commission File No. 001-36629 (Q3 10-Q page:1). The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank; blank is not evidence of absence.
- Holding company: `We are a holding company, and our only significant assets are ownership interests in our subsidiaries.` (Q3 10-Q page:50).

- Debt issuers: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (CEI) is the borrower under the CEI Credit Agreement and the issuer of the CEI notes (Q3 10-Q page:17 and page:19 to page:20). CEI debt is guaranteed by `each existing and future material wholly owned domestic subsidiary` (page:21). The guarantor names and the restricted-group definition are not in the supplied text.

- Separate borrower group: Caesars Virginia, LLC is the borrower under the CVA facilities, which are secured by its assets; `CEI does not provide a guarantee of these facilities.` (Q3 10-Q page:21). CEI holds a `50.0% variable interest` in CVA Holdco, LLC and consolidates it as primary beneficiary, with a minority interest (page:29). Consolidated debt therefore includes debt that is not guaranteed by the parent.

- Lease counterparties: VICI Properties L.P. (the VICI Leases) and GLP Capital, L.P. (the GLPI Leases) (Q3 10-Q page:36). The leases are accounted for as failed sale-leasebacks and appear in `Long-term financing obligations`, separate from `Long-term debt` on the balance sheet (page:2).

- Acquirer: the Merger Agreement parties are Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and Empire Merger Sub, Inc. (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases instead name `Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` as the company that will acquire Caesars (Q3 release page:4). The 10-Q heading also reads `Proposed Merger of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. with Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` The relationship between Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. and Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC is not explained in the supplied text. It is an unresolved identity distinction, carried as a gap.
- Noncontrolling interests: shown in the statements (Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:4); the relevant partner is the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians for Caesars Virginia (page:29).
### Version relationships and conflicts

- Each 10-Q is a separate period report; the Q3 10-Q does not restate the Q1 or Q2 reports. Each release duplicates statement tables from its own 10-Q. The 10-Q controls for statement facts; the release is supporting.

- Net debt and the debt split by bank debt and notes appear only in the releases (Q3 release page:2). The 10-Q debt note gives face value, book value and fair value by instrument (Q3 10-Q page:15 to page:16). The two are different presentations of different measures, and they are not treated as a conflict.
- Naming difference on the acquirer: see Identity and perimeter. Effect: CP-1A must name the signatory entity from the 10-Q and flag the releases' label as management wording.
- No draft, unsigned or superseded source is in the pack. All filings carry signature dates.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, segment results, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, debt, cash flows, cash interest | 10-K page:99 to page:101 and page:121 to page:122; Q3 10-Q page:2 to page:5, page:15 to page:16, page:30 to page:34, page:49 to page:50; releases page:1 to page:7 | Interim statements are unaudited. Financing obligations are a large liability class outside debt. Lease note exists only in the 10-K. Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026 and the Grand Bazaar purchase limit comparability (Q3 10-Q page:10 to page:11). |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, properties, history, merger terms, ownership and joint ventures | Q3 10-Q page:6 to page:10, page:29 to page:31, page:36 to page:39; 10-K Business section from page:4 | Merger Agreement, proxy statement and merger financing not supplied. Acquirer naming difference unresolved. |

| CP-2 | Debt by instrument, maturities, guarantees, covenants, liquidity, lease burden | Q3 10-Q page:15 to page:21 and page:50 to page:53; 10-K page:79, page:115 to page:117 | No executed agreements. Covenant levels are printed but covenant ratio values are not. Lease payment schedule is at December 31, 2025 only. |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims across modules | All seven sources carry page locators | Text extraction only; no check against filed HTML or XBRL. |
### Source-profile review

- Financial reports: statements, period labels and units are present and consistent. The Q3 10-Q labels columns `Three Months Ended September 30` and `Nine Months Ended September 30`, so discrete-quarter and year-to-date figures are separable for Q3. Discrete Q2 figures come from the Q2 filing's own three-month column. Year-to-date cash-flow figures are cumulative, so a discrete quarter cash flow needs subtraction of earlier year-to-date reports; that step belongs to downstream modules.
- Debt table: Q3 10-Q page:15 to page:16 lists 12 debt lines by facility, with face value and book value, rate and final maturity. Facility-level carrying values are therefore present.
- Cash paid for interest and taxes: Q3 10-Q page:5 gives `Cash interest paid for debt`, cash interest paid for rent on the GLPI and VICI Leases, and `Income taxes paid, net`.

- Covenants: levels are printed for the CEI Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan A, and for the CVA facilities, with a statement that the company `was in compliance with all of the applicable financial covenants` (Q3 10-Q page:21). The reported ratio values are not printed.

- Earnings releases: reported and adjusted figures, quarter and nine-month columns, an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and a net debt reconciliation are present. No guidance is given in the Q3 release text, and no conference call is held (page:4).
- Legal and financing sources: no executed credit agreement, indenture, lease or merger agreement is supplied. They are described in the filings only.

- Workbooks, scans, images and decks: none supplied. The pack has no presentation; the releases stand in for decks. The Q3 10-Q page:37 refers to a map of Caesars Digital presence; the map image is not in the text, which is recorded as a parse gap.
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: one audited annual report, three unaudited interim reports and three releases cover FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 with prior-year comparatives. Together they support a financial foundation, a debt and lease map, and the merger narrative up to October 27, 2026.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the pending acquisition can change ownership and leverage. The Q3 10-Q lists `risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction` (page:57) and `the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all`. The supplied text does not say how the existing CEI debt or the CVA facilities are treated at closing.

- Source risk mechanism: lease payments to VICI and GLPI run through `Long-term financing obligations` and interest expense, not through the debt table, and Adjusted EBITDA `excludes the expense associated with certain of our leases` (Q3 release page:3). A consumer reading only total debt or Adjusted EBITDA would understate fixed claims and overstate coverage. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must carry the lease obligations and the lease cash interest alongside debt.

- Second mechanism: the covenant definitions govern headroom, and the company states that its Adjusted EBITDA definition `may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt or lease agreements` (Q3 10-Q page:49). Consequence: CP-2 can report printed levels and the compliance statement but cannot verify headroom.

- What cannot proceed: merger financing analysis, post-closing capital structure, covenant headroom on agreement definitions, guarantor-level and restricted-group analysis, and any event after October 27, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Merger Agreement (Form 8-K filed May 28, 2026, Exhibit 2.1), the merger proxy statement filed August 26, 2026, any financing commitment papers, the CEI Credit Agreement and indentures, and the VICI and GLPI lease agreements; and any filing dated October 28, 2026 to November 5, 2026.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Counts of pages and debt lines above are coverage counts taken from the pinned files and the debt table.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Merger Agreement, proxy statement and merger financing not supplied; treatment of existing debt at closing not described | High | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply Form 8-K Exhibit 2.1 of May 28, 2026, the proxy statement filed August 26, 2026 and any financing commitments |

| Acquirer naming differs: Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC in the 10-Q, Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. in the releases and the 10-Q heading; relationship not explained | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Confirm from the Merger Agreement or proxy statement |
| Executed credit agreement, indentures and VICI and GLPI leases not supplied | High for legal work; Medium for CP-2 | CP-2 | Supply executed documents and amendments |
| Covenant ratio values not printed; only thresholds and a compliance statement | Medium | CP-2 | Supply compliance certificates or agreement definitions |

| Lease note and payment schedule exist only in the 10-K at December 31, 2025; the 10-Qs show the aggregate financing obligation line only | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Label lease detail as of December 31, 2025 and carry the aggregate balance for later dates |
| Guarantor names and restricted-group definition not in the supplied text | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the exhibit of subsidiary guarantors and the indenture definitions |
| Nothing supplied between October 27, 2026 and 2026-11-05 | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply any later Form 8-K or confirm none |
| Text extraction only; filed HTML and XBRL not compared; the Caesars Digital map is not in the text | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML when available |
| No rating reports, market prices or peer data in the pack | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Not required for this scope; keep Not supplied |
## Next module

- CP-1: treat the 10-K and 10-Qs as controlling for statements; keep audited FY2025, unaudited Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and nine-month periods separate; keep debt, financing obligations and lease cash interest separate; label net debt and Adjusted EBITDA as company non-GAAP; note the March 3, 2026 Windsor consolidation and May 1, 2026 Grand Bazaar purchase as comparability breaks.

- CP-1A: carry the pending merger as the central transaction, with signing on May 27, 2026, announcement on May 28, 2026 and stockholder approval on September 22, 2026; name the signatory entity from the 10-Q and flag the acquirer naming difference; label anything after October 27, 2026 as Not supplied.

- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing merger financing, executed documents, covenant ratio values and the December 31, 2025 date of the lease schedule as restrictions; keep CVA debt separate because CEI does not guarantee it.

## Request

- Issuer: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id `czr`), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05. Reporting currency USD, all amounts in US$ millions as the filings print them (`(In millions)`). Current period Q3 2026; prior period FY2025 (context).
- Run: `czr-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`. Execution: host session; the host read the pinned page text and wrote this answer. No provider was called.

- Perimeter: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, including the 50.0% variable interest in CVA Holdco, LLC that it consolidates. Debt, Adjusted EBITDA, interest and cash flow figures below are on that consolidated perimeter. The parent has no separate statements in the pack.

- Question: what is the reported financial base for the credit view, with debt, leases outside debt, liquidity, maturities, coverage and the covenant picture, for FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026?

- Locators are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text of each source, not printed page numbers. Periods are labelled FY2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026, nine months 2026 (9M 2026), nine months 2025 (9M 2025) and LTM Q3 2026.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported debt is 3.26x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, but lease financing obligations of 13,188 sit outside debt; including them leverage is 6.95x and cash interest cover is only 1.69x. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a company non-GAAP measure and covenant ratio values are not printed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Debt fell from 11,905 at FY2025 to 11,659 at Q3 2026, with the revolver undrawn at quarter-end. | Modest deleveraging; debt-only leverage moved from 3.29x to 3.26x. | High |
| Lease rent interest of about 1,371 over the last twelve months is paid on top of 741 of cash interest on debt. | Fixed charges absorb most Adjusted EBITDA, leaving thin cover. | Medium |
| Net loss attributable to Caesars was (283) for nine months 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA fell to 2,672 from 2,723. | Earnings are shrinking while fixed charges are stable. | Medium |

| Liquidity was 2,947 on the company basis at Q3 2026, and maturities rise to 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030. | Near-term liquidity is adequate; the 2029 and 2030 wall is the pressure point. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The reported base supports a debt-only view and a lease-inclusive view, and the two give very different pictures. On the company's own measures, debt is 11,659 at Q3 2026 (face value), net debt is 10,795, and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 3,573, giving 3.26x and 3.02x. But Adjusted EBITDA is stated before the rent on the VICI and GLPI leases, which the company accounts for as financing obligations of 13,188 outside debt. Adding those obligations lifts leverage to 6.95x, and adding the roughly 1,371 of rent cash interest to the 741 of cash interest on debt gives cash interest cover of 1.69x. Both views use the same company Adjusted EBITDA, so neither is a covenant ratio. Earnings are drifting lower (Adjusted EBITDA 2,672 for 9M 2026 against 2,723 for 9M 2025, with Las Vegas down and Regional and Digital up) and net loss attributable to Caesars widened to (283) from (252). Liquidity is adequate in the near term and nothing in the debt table matures before 2028 beyond amortisation. The pending acquisition adds uncertainty about the debt, but the supplied sources do not say how existing debt is treated.

The CEI Senior Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 8, 2025 (10-K page:80), so they are not outstanding at FY2025. Interest rate on the term loans: Term SOFR plus a margin of 2.25% (Q3 10-Q page:18 to page:19); weighted average rates were 6.12% on variable and 6.18% on fixed rate debt, with variable-rate borrowings of $5.8 billion, about 50% of debt (page:54).
### Leases and other claims outside debt

- Financing obligations: `Long-term financing obligations` were 13,188 at September 30, 2026, 13,157 at June 30, 2026, 13,126 at March 31, 2026 and 13,096 at December 31, 2025 (balance sheets, page:2). They arise from failed sale-leasebacks with VICI and GLPI. The 10-K splits them at December 31, 2025 as GLPI Leases 1,284 and VICI Leases 11,705 (10-K page:117), which total 12,989; the remaining 107 of the 13,096 balance is not itemised in the text read. The 10-Qs give no split.

- Why the balance grows: `cash payments are less than the interest expense recognized, which causes the failed-sale leaseback obligation to increase during the initial years of the lease term` (10-K page:118). The increase from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 is 92 (calculated).

- Rent cash: cash interest paid for rent was 1,349 in FY2025 and 1,030 for GLPI and VICI in 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). Management estimates `approximately $345 million` of lease payments to VICI and GLPI for the remainder of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:51) and `approximately $1.4 billion` for 2026 (10-K page:80).

- Contractual terms: VICI leases have a 15-year initial term with four five-year renewals, CPI escalators with a 2% floor and a net revenue variable element; the next variable adjustment year begins in November 2027 (10-K page:116; Q3 10-Q page:51). The GLPI Master Lease runs through September 2038 with escalators (10-K page:117). The lease covenants require a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1 for the GLPI Leases (Q3 10-Q page:52).

- Operating and finance leases: operating lease liability 742 and finance lease liabilities 147 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:115 and page:116). The 10-Qs show no update beyond 203 of right-of-use assets obtained in exchange for lease liabilities in 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5); the filing does not state which lease it relates to. Separately, the Caesars Windsor lease has annual minimum rent of about 19 (Q3 10-Q page:10).

- Other commitments: sports sponsorship obligations 309 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15); self-insurance liability 244 (page:15). Defined-benefit plans are small: the Tropicana Atlantic City plan had assets of 33 and obligations of 22, and the Scioto Downs plan about 1 each (10-K page:140). Multi-employer pension plan participation exists (10-K page:141); withdrawal liability amounts were not found. No factoring or supply-chain finance programme was found in the pack.

- Litigation and the data incident: the 10-K states the `Data Incident` has not had a material impact (10-K page:121); Q3 2026 litigation liabilities are `not material` (Q3 10-Q page:15). Merger-related suits have been threatened or filed (Q3 10-Q page:65), with no amount.

Locators: Q3 10-Q page:20 to page:21 and page:52 to page:53. The company states it `was in compliance with all of the applicable financial covenants described above` at September 30, 2026. After repayment of Term Loan A, the revolver covenants are tested only when testing conditions are satisfied (page:20). The ratios computed in this answer use company Adjusted EBITDA and face debt; they are not covenant ratios, because the covenant definitions are not supplied and the company says its Adjusted EBITDA definition `may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt or lease agreements` (Q3 10-Q page:49). A reader must not compare 6.95x or 1.69x with 6.50:1 or 2.0:1.
### Events, comparability and subsequent events

- Pending merger: the Merger Agreement was signed May 27, 2026; consideration is `$31.00` per share in cash plus a ticking fee after June 26, 2027; stockholders approved on September 22, 2026; a termination fee of $200 million and a reverse termination fee of $450 million are described; the initial end date is May 27, 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:7 to page:9). The sources do not describe merger financing or the treatment of existing debt. Merger costs were 12 for Q3 2026 and 22 for 9M 2026 (page:10).

- Comparability: Caesars Windsor was consolidated into Regional from March 3, 2026 (purchased net assets included about 42 of furniture and equipment and 12 of net working capital); the Grand Bazaar interest was acquired on May 1, 2026 for about 66 including 10 deferred (Q3 10-Q page:10). The company states that the periods after these purchases are `not fully comparable` with earlier periods (Q3 10-Q page:11). Cash paid for asset acquisitions was 98 in 9M 2026.

- Financing events in 2026: the revolver was repaid from 160 to nil; 9M 2026 proceeds from long-term debt and revolving facilities were 1,335 and repayments 1,581 (Q3 10-Q page:4 to page:5). There was no share repurchase in 9M 2026 against 179 in 9M 2025; 221 of authorisation remains but `no share repurchases are expected` (page:53).
- Earlier: the 546 CEI Senior Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 8, 2025 with revolver borrowings and note receivable proceeds (10-K page:80).
- Events after September 30, 2026 up to the cutoff: none stated in the Q3 10-Q; nothing is supplied after October 27, 2026.
### Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication

- Earnings: Adjusted EBITDA for 9M 2026 is 2,672 against 2,723, with Las Vegas 1,179 against 1,281 and Regional 1,447 against 1,385 (Q3 10-Q page:31 to page:32). The Las Vegas decline is attributed to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation (Q3 10-Q page:46). Credit implication: the large Las Vegas segment, which carries the VICI Las Vegas lease, is the weak spot, and Regional growth includes the Windsor consolidation.

- Fixed charges: Adjusted EBITDA is before lease rent, so the lease cash interest of about 1,371 is a charge ahead of any debt service. Cash interest on debt is 741 and net loss attributable to Caesars is (533) over the last twelve months; interest expense, net of 2,287 exceeds operating income of 1,801 over the same period, and it includes lease interest. Credit implication: cover on all fixed charges is thin even though debt-only leverage looks moderate.

- Cash generation: 9M 2026 operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment is 435 against 350, helped by lower capital expenditure (507 against 648) rather than higher operating cash (942 against 998). Credit implication: free cash flow depends on capital expenditure discipline; the 4.99% ratio to debt is low for the leverage.

- Liquidity and maturities: liquidity on the company basis is 2,947 including cash of 864, with the revolver undrawn. Debt maturing before 2029 is small (28 in remaining 2026, 114 in 2027, 646 in 2028), then 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030. Credit implication: refinancing risk concentrates in 2029 and 2030, and the revolver and Term Loan A mature January 31, 2028, about fifteen months after the as-of date.

- Quality of the evidence: the quarterly statements are unaudited. The FY2025 statements are audited: the auditor states they `present fairly, in all material respects` the financial position and results (10-K page:96), in a report dated February 17, 2026 (10-K page:98). Adjusted EBITDA, net debt and the cash-interest lines are management or supplemental presentations; the 10-K labels Adjusted EBITDA as unaudited (10-K page:77).
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ millions from the cited pages. "LTM" means last twelve months and is calculated as FY2025 plus the year-to-date 2026 amount minus the year-to-date 2025 amount of the same length.
### LTM Adjusted EBITDA
- Discrete quarters tie: 887 + 920 + 865 = 2,672.
### LTM and discrete cash flow and income lines
- Net loss attributable LTM: -502 + -283 - -252 = -533. Quarters: -98 + -62 + -123 = -283.

- LTM operating cash flow and purchases at Q1 and Q2: Q1 operating cash flow 1,302 + 204 - 218 = 1,288 and purchases 805 + 168 - 223 = 750; Q2 operating cash flow 1,302 + 675 - 680 = 1,297 and purchases 805 + 335 - 453 = 687.
### Leverage, cover and cash flow ratios
### Liquidity
- Q3 2026: 864 + 2,250 + 25 - 96 - 40 - 56 = 2,947 (matches release page:2); availability 2,083. Net of letters of credit only: 2,250 + 25 - 96 = 2,179.
- Letters of credit are reported against the CEI revolver (Q3 10-Q page:19); none is reported against the CVA revolver, which has a 10 letter of credit sub-facility.
### Tie-outs

### Business and transaction view

The credit story is a large, lease-heavy casino operator with a diversified but physically concentrated revenue base, entering a change of control on terms the sources describe only in part. Regional properties and Las Vegas supply about 85% of net revenues, Caesars Digital is the growing third leg, and the VICI and GLPI real estate leases make the company a tenant at 25 of the 47 casinos it owns or leases. Ownership today is public, with about 273 holders of record, no sponsor named in the context and no dividend history. The pending merger converts each share into cash of $31.00 plus a ticking fee after June 26, 2027, was approved by stockholders on September 22, 2026, and remains subject to antitrust and gaming approvals with an outside date that can run to November 27, 2027. For creditors, the open questions are who finances the purchase, whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, and whether leverage rises; the sources state that financing risk exists but give no terms. Until the Merger Agreement, proxy statement and financing papers are supplied, the transaction can be described but not assessed for debt effects.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction is a pending cash acquisition of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. On May 27, 2026 the company, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, Empire Merger Sub, Inc., Landry's Fertitta, LLC (for Section 9.14 of the agreement only) and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. (for Section 9.14(j) only) signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which Merger Sub merges into the company and the company survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases state that the agreement is with `Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` and that it was announced on May 28, 2026 (Q3 release page:4). The two names are logged below as an unresolved conflict. Each share other than excluded, parent rollover and dissenting shares converts into $31.00 in cash plus, if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day from the first day of the following month; parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, and the sources do not disclose a rollover percentage (Q3 10-Q page:7). Restricted stock units are cancelled for cash at the same consideration (Q3 10-Q page:7).

The status is stockholder-approved and awaiting regulatory conditions. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and the proposals were approved at a special meeting on September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Closing remains conditioned on expiry or termination of the HSR Act waiting period and receipt of certain gaming regulatory approvals; the filings do not say which approvals have been received (Q3 10-Q page:8 and page:62). The initial end date is May 27, 2027, extended automatically to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only those regulatory conditions remain open (Q3 10-Q page:8). A termination fee of $200 million is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a reverse termination fee of $450 million by Fertitta Gaming in others, including antitrust or gaming law prohibitions or the end date occurring with only regulatory conditions open (Q3 10-Q page:9). A no-shop has applied since July 11, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:8). On completion the common stock is delisted from NASDAQ and deregistered, which ends the public filings that this credit view relies on (Q3 10-Q page:10).

For debt, the sources give no use of proceeds, sources and uses, new debt raised, financing commitments, equity contribution or liquidity effect. The filings list `risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction` and `the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all` among forward-looking risks (Q3 10-Q page:57), and the company represented its `present debt financing and covenants` in the agreement (Q3 10-Q page:8). They do not state whether the existing CEI Credit Agreement, the CEI notes or the CVA facilities are repaid, assumed, amended or subject to a change-of-control offer at closing. That absence is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The company incurred transaction costs related to the merger of 10 for Q2 2026 and 12 for Q3 2026, 22 for nine months 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Q3 10-Q page:10).

New debt issues: none appear in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The debt table lists no instrument issued in 2026, and proceeds from long-term debt and revolving credit facilities of 1,335 against repayments of 1,581 reflect revolver activity and scheduled repayment (Q3 10-Q page:5). The last term debt issues in the filings are the CEI Senior Notes due 2032 of $1.1 billion at 6.00% on October 17, 2024, the CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2032 of $1.5 billion at 6.50% and the CEI Term Loan B-1 of $2.9 billion on February 6, 2024, and the Caesars Virginia facilities of April 26, 2024 (Q3 10-Q page:18 to page:20). The CEI Senior Notes due 2027 of $546 million were redeemed on July 8, 2025 with revolver borrowings and note proceeds (10-K page:80). Merger-related debt is not described.

## Calculations
All figures are US$ millions from the cited pages unless a percentage or count.

- Segment shares of FY2025 net revenues of 11,486: Las Vegas 4,049 / 11,486 = 35.3%; Regional 5,756 / 11,486 = 50.1%; Caesars Digital 1,408 / 11,486 = 12.3%; Managed and Branded 279 / 11,486 = 2.4%. Corporate and Other is (6). Sum of segments and Corporate and Other: 4,049 + 5,756 + 1,408 + 279 - 6 = 11,486.
- Regional plus Las Vegas share: (4,049 + 5,756) / 11,486 = 85.4%, rounded to about 85% in the view.
- Segment Adjusted EBITDA margins FY2025: Las Vegas 1,728 / 4,049 = 42.7%; Regional 1,789 / 5,756 = 31.1%; Caesars Digital 236 / 1,408 = 16.8%; Managed and Branded 67 / 279 = 24.0%.
- Revenue mix FY2025 check: casino 6,617 / 11,486 = 57.6% (about 58% stated); food and beverage 1,714 / 11,486 = 14.9% (about 15%); hotel 1,945 / 11,486 = 16.9% (about 17%).

- 9M 2026 segment revenue changes against 9M 2025: Las Vegas 2,950 - 3,009 = -59; Regional 4,627 - 4,359 = 268; Caesars Digital 1,051 - 989 = 62; Managed and Branded 181 - 214 = -33; total 8,803 - 8,570 = 233.
- Merger costs: 10 for Q2 2026 plus 12 for Q3 2026 = 22 for nine months 2026, matching the Q3 10-Q.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

The pending acquisition leaves the future of the existing debt open. | Medium | Merger financing, covenant ratio values and the debt documents are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Liquidity was USD 2,947 million at Q3 2026 with the revolver undrawn, and no notes mature before 2029. | The near-term cushion is adequate, and the refinancing pressure is in 2029 and 2030. | Medium |
| Lease financing obligations of USD 13,188 million sit outside debt and take leverage to 6.95x. | Fixed lease claims outweigh the debt claims and limit room to absorb weaker earnings. | Medium |

| Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 2,672 million against USD 2,723 million, with Las Vegas weaker and Regional and Digital stronger. | Earnings are slipping while fixed charges are stable. | Medium |

| The acquisition needs antitrust and gaming approvals, and the sources do not describe its financing or how existing debt is treated. | Change-of-control effects on the notes and loans cannot be assessed. | Low |
### Credit view

Caesars Entertainment, Inc. is a liquid but lease-burdened credit: debt-only leverage of 3.26x looks moderate, yet fixed-charge cover is thin and the change of control leaves the debt outlook open. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,947 million, an undrawn revolver and a first notes maturity only in 2029. The weakest point is fixed charges: USD 13,188 million of lease financing obligations sit outside debt, lifting leverage to 6.95x and holding cash interest cover to 1.69x while Adjusted EBITDA slipped to USD 2,672 million for nine months 2026. What decides the outcome is how the pending acquisition is financed and whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, which the supplied sources do not say.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental view: adequate liquidity and a moderate debt-only profile, offset by thin all-in fixed-charge cover, softening Las Vegas earnings and an unresolved change of control. Not a rating and not a recommendation. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium (below High because the merger financing, covenant definitions and agreements are not supplied) | CP-1 debt, lease, liquidity and ratio figures; CP-1A transaction, segment and governance rows |
### Key findings

First, liquidity is adequate. Caesars Entertainment, Inc. held USD 864 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,083 million of revolver availability on the company basis at September 30, 2026, together USD 2,947 million, and the CEI revolver was undrawn after USD 160 million was drawn at December 31, 2025 [CP-1]. No notes mature before 2029. Debt falling due is USD 28 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 114 million in 2027 and USD 646 million in 2028, which is mostly the CEI Term Loan A of USD 609 million; the CEI revolver and that term loan both mature on January 31, 2028. Nothing matures within twelve months of the as-of date beyond scheduled amortisation, so the 2028 date becomes a current-year issue from early 2027 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Second, the lease structure is the main fixed claim. Long-term financing obligations to VICI and GLPI of USD 13,188 million sit outside the USD 11,659 million of debt, and the lease payment schedule at December 31, 2025 shows USD 1,392 million in 2027, USD 1,424 million in 2028 and USD 1,446 million in 2029 [CP-1; annual report]. Lease cash interest of about USD 1,371 million over the last twelve months compares with USD 741 million of cash interest on debt. Adjusted EBITDA excludes this rent, so total debt plus financing obligations over Adjusted EBITDA is 6.95x against 3.26x for debt alone, and Adjusted EBITDA over all cash interest is 1.69x. Adjusted EBITDA less purchases of property and equipment of USD 664 million gives USD 2,909 million against USD 2,112 million of cash interest, or 1.38x (calculated). Net loss attributable to Caesars was USD 533 million over the last twelve months.

Third, leverage is flat to slightly better on debt and slightly worse once leases are counted. Debt-only leverage moved from 3.29x at FY2025 to 3.26x at Q3 2026 as debt fell by USD 246 million, while the lease-inclusive ratio moved from 6.90x to 6.95x because the financing obligation grew by USD 92 million and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 3,624 million to USD 3,573 million [CP-1]. The company explains that in the early years of these leases cash payments are below the interest expense recognised, so the obligation increases.

Fourth, earnings are mixed by segment. Las Vegas Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,179 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,281 million, attributed by the company to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation, while Regional rose to USD 1,447 million from USD 1,385 million, helped by the Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026, and Caesars Digital rose to USD 181 million from USD 151 million [CP-1; CP-1A]. Las Vegas carries the highest segment margin, so its softness weighs more than its revenue share of 35.3% suggests (Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, refinancing risk is concentrated. Maturities of USD 1,574 million in 2029 and USD 3,962 million in 2030 together are USD 5,536 million, 47.5% of face debt of USD 11,659 million, and variable-rate borrowings of USD 5.8 billion are about half of debt with no derivatives held [CP-1]. A move of 1.00% in the base rate would change annual cash interest on that variable debt by about USD 58 million (calculated, before any floors), against USD 741 million of cash interest on debt over the last twelve months.

Sixth, the pending acquisition is the largest open item. The agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at USD 31.00 per share in cash, stockholders approved it on September 22, 2026, and closing needs antitrust and gaming approvals, with an initial end date of May 27, 2027, extendable to November 27, 2027 [CP-1A]. A USD 200 million fee is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a USD 450 million fee by the buyer in others. The sources do not describe merger financing, the equity contribution, rollover terms or the treatment of the CEI Credit Agreement, the notes or the Caesars Virginia facilities at closing. That is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding (Insufficient Information).

Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The CEI revolver and Term Loan A carry a maximum net total leverage ratio of 6.50:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 2.0:1, the Caesars Virginia facilities 4:1 and 1.05:1, and the GLPI Leases a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1, with compliance stated at September 30, 2026 but no ratio values printed. The ratios computed here are not covenant ratios and must not be compared with those levels (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity and no near-term maturity wall: USD 2,947 million of liquidity against USD 142 million of scheduled principal through 2027, with the revolver undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Diversified footprint and a growing digital segment: 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions, Regional at 50.1% and Las Vegas at 35.3% of FY2025 net revenues, and Caesars Digital Adjusted EBITDA up to USD 181 million for nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (3) Conservative capital return and debt direction: no cash dividends, no share repurchases in nine months 2026, debt down USD 246 million since FY2025 and asset sale proceeds applied to redeeming the 2027 notes (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Moderate debt-only leverage of 3.26x and debt-only cash interest cover of 4.82x (Analyst Interpretation on company Adjusted EBITDA; CP-1). (5) Stockholder approval of the merger removes one execution uncertainty (Documentary Fact; CP-1A).

Weaknesses. (1) Fixed lease claims outside debt: USD 13,188 million of financing obligations and about USD 1,371 million a year of rent cash interest, leaving all-in cover of 1.69x and lease-inclusive leverage of 6.95x (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Earnings drift and net losses: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,672 million against USD 2,723 million and a net loss attributable to Caesars of USD 283 million for nine months 2026, with the Las Vegas segment, which has the highest margin, declining (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (3) Refinancing concentration in 2029 and 2030 of USD 5,536 million and about half of debt at floating rates (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (4) Opaque post-closing structure: merger financing and debt treatment undisclosed, and the buyer named differently in the filings and the releases (Insufficient Information; CP-1A). (5) Covenant and agreement evidence missing: levels printed without ratio values, definitions or executed documents (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1). (6) The Adjusted EBITDA add-backs, including transaction costs and other of USD 64 million for nine months 2026, are management defined, and the company says its definition may differ from those in its debt and lease agreements (Management Language; CP-1).
### Debt and claims inventory
| Claim | Amount (US$m) | Date | Inside the debt figure? | Security, guarantors, maturity | Locator |
| CEI Revolving Credit Facility (2,250 commitment) | 0 drawn | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; subsidiary guarantors; January 31, 2028 | Q3 10-Q page:15 and page:17 |
| CEI Term Loan A | 609 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; subsidiary guarantors; January 31, 2028 | Q3 10-Q page:15 and page:18 |

| CEI Term Loan B-1 | 2,828 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; subsidiary guarantors; February 6, 2031 | Q3 10-Q page:16 and page:19 |
| CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2030 (7.00%) | 2,000 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; subsidiary guarantors; February 15, 2030 | Q3 10-Q page:16 and page:19 |
| CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2032 (6.50%) | 1,500 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; subsidiary guarantors; February 15, 2032 | Q3 10-Q page:16 and page:20 |
| CEI Senior Notes due 2029 (4.625%) | 1,200 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior unsecured; subsidiary guarantors; October 15, 2029 | Q3 10-Q page:16 and page:20 |
| CEI Senior Notes due 2032 (6.00%) | 1,100 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior unsecured; subsidiary guarantors; October 15, 2032 | Q3 10-Q page:16 and page:20 |

| CVA Delayed Draw Term Loan (up to 400) and CVA Revolving Credit Facility (25, undrawn) | 371 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Secured by Caesars Virginia assets; no CEI guarantee; April 26, 2029 | Q3 10-Q page:15, page:19 and page:21 |
| Special Improvement District Bonds (4.30%) and long-term notes and other payables | 39 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Bonds due 2037; security not stated | Q3 10-Q page:16 |
| Total debt (face value) | 11,659 | Sept 30, 2026 | n/a | Book value 11,563 | Q3 10-Q page:16 |

| Long-term financing obligations (VICI and GLPI failed sale-leasebacks) | 13,188 | Sept 30, 2026 | No | VICI Leases (18 casinos) and GLPI Leases (six casinos); at December 31, 2025 GLPI 1,284 and VICI 11,705, 107 not itemised | Q3 10-Q page:2 and page:36; 10-K page:117 |
| Operating lease liability | 742 | Dec 31, 2025 | No | Real estate and equipment leases | 10-K page:115 |
| Finance lease liabilities | 147 | Dec 31, 2025 | No | Equipment and real estate | 10-K page:116 |
| Sports sponsorship and partnership obligations | 309 | Sept 30, 2026 | No | Contracts through 2040 | Q3 10-Q page:15 |
| Self-insurance liability | 244 | Sept 30, 2026 | No | Within accrued other liabilities | Q3 10-Q page:15 |

| Litigation and the Data Incident | Not material | Sept 30, 2026 | No | Company states liabilities are not material | Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:121 |

No factoring or supply-chain finance programme was found in the seven sources. Debt maturities by year at September 30, 2026 (US$m): remainder of 2026 28, 2027 114, 2028 646, 2029 1,574, 2030 3,962, thereafter 5,335 (Q3 10-Q page:16). Estimated interest payments follow in the same table: 160, 780, 740, 700, 440 and 300 (total 3,120), giving total debt service of 188, 894, 1,386, 2,274, 4,402 and 5,635.
### Liquidity by facility
| Component (US$m) | Q3 2026 | Locator |
| Cash and cash equivalents (unrestricted) | 864 | Q3 10-Q page:2 |
| CEI Revolving Credit Facility commitment, undrawn | 2,250 | Q3 10-Q page:50 |
| less letters of credit drawn on it | (96) | Q3 10-Q page:19 and page:50 |
| less reserves for specific permitted uses | (40) | Q3 10-Q page:17 and page:50 |
| less regulatory commitment | (56) | Q3 10-Q page:19 and page:50 |
| CVA Revolving Credit Facility commitment, undrawn | 25 | Q3 10-Q page:50 |
| Total liquidity on the company basis | 2,947 | Q3 release page:2 |
| Of which revolver availability | 2,083 | Calculated |
| Restricted cash, excluded | 94 | Q3 10-Q page:2 |

No facility expires within twelve months of the as-of date: the CEI revolver matures on January 31, 2028 and the CVA revolver on April 26, 2029. Restricted cash and the 40 and 56 held back are not counted as free liquidity in the company's own table.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Fixed charge burden of leases | Rent is paid ahead of debt service and is not in Adjusted EBITDA; the financing obligation rises while payments are below recognised interest | Thin all-in cover of 1.69x means a modest EBITDA decline sharply reduces cover; lessor remedies are not supplied | Critical |

| Change of control and undisclosed financing | Buyer financing and the treatment of existing debt are not described; the filings list the risk of increased leverage | Debt could be repaid, assumed or re-levered; the outcome cannot be judged from the sources | Critical |
| Las Vegas softening | Convention and leisure visitation fall, hotel occupancy 89.1% against 91.6% in Q3 2026 | Highest-margin segment, tied to the VICI Las Vegas lease, weakens | Material |

| Refinancing in 2029 and 2030 | USD 5,536 million falls due in two years and about half of debt floats | Market access and rates decide the cost; a stable owner or a deal failure changes who bears it | Material |
| Covenant visibility | Levels printed, ratios not; Adjusted EBITDA definition differs from agreements | Headroom is unknown; an EBITDA decline could reach a test not visible here | Material |

| Regulatory and execution risk of the merger | Antitrust and gaming approvals, possible asset sales, litigation | Delay or failure extends the standalone case; a USD 200 million fee could fall on the company | Material |
### Event calendar after the as-of date
| Date | Event | Source note |
| Nov 2026 | VICI lease CPI escalation takes effect each November | Q3 10-Q page:51 |
| Feb 2027 | The CEI revolver and Term Loan A (maturity January 31, 2028) fall within twelve months | Q3 10-Q page:18 |
| May 27, 2027 | Initial end date of the Merger Agreement (extendable to Aug 27 and Nov 27, 2027) | Q3 10-Q page:8 |
| June 26, 2027 | Ticking fee date for merger consideration | Q3 10-Q page:7 |
| Nov 2027 | Next VICI variable rent adjustment lease year begins | Q3 10-Q page:51 |
These are contract terms and scheduled dates, not events that have occurred. Nothing is supplied after October 27, 2026.
## Calculations
All inputs in USD millions from CP-1 or the cited pages. Ratios are on company Adjusted EBITDA and face debt and are not covenant ratios.
- Revolver availability, company basis, Q3 2026: 2,250 - 96 - 40 - 56 + 25 = 2,083; plus cash 864 = 2,947 (matches the Q3 release).
- Scheduled principal through 2027: 28 + 114 = 142.
- Variable-rate sensitivity: 5,800 x 1.00% = 58 per year, before floors and with no derivatives; 58 / 741 = 7.8% of last-twelve-months cash interest on debt.
- Adjusted EBITDA less purchases of property and equipment, last twelve months: 3,573 - 664 = 2,909. Cover of all cash interest: 2,909 / (741 + 1,371) = 2,909 / 2,112 = 1.38x.
- Cash fixed charges over Adjusted EBITDA: (741 + 1,371) / 3,573 = 59.1%.

- Lease payments by year at December 31, 2025 (GLPI Leases plus VICI Leases): 2027 117 + 1,275 = 1,392; 2028 119 + 1,305 = 1,424; 2029 120 + 1,326 = 1,446; 2030 122 + 1,346 = 1,468; total future payments 4,719 + 48,140 = 52,859. Contract totals, not commitments to pay in those exact amounts after escalators.
- Lease and debt service for 2027: 894 (debt service at September 30, 2026) + 1,392 (lease payments at December 31, 2025) = 2,286; the two dates differ.
- Leverage change: debt 11,905 - 11,659 = 246; financing obligation 13,188 - 13,096 = 92; LTM Adjusted EBITDA 3,573 versus 3,624 = -51.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Merger financing, equity contribution, rollover terms and treatment of existing debt not supplied | Determines post-closing leverage and whether existing debt survives | Credit view, refinancing | High | Obtain the Merger Agreement exhibit, proxy statement and financing commitments |

| Covenant ratio values and definitions not supplied | Headroom cannot be measured; computed ratios are not covenant ratios | Covenant risk | High | Obtain compliance certificates and the CEI Credit Agreement |

| Executed credit agreement, indentures and VICI and GLPI leases not supplied | Lessor remedies, cross-defaults, change-of-control and lease covenant terms unknown | Structure, claims | High | Obtain executed documents and amendments |

| Lease detail by landlord only at December 31, 2025; 107 of the 13,096 balance not itemised | Later lease cash and balance split cannot be built | Fixed charge analysis | Medium | Request later lease schedule |
| Acquirer identity: Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC against Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. | Obligor and support analysis after closing | Change of control | Medium | Confirm from the Merger Agreement |
| Regulatory approvals received to date not stated; nothing supplied after October 27, 2026 | Timing of closing | Event calendar | Medium | Obtain later Form 8-K filings |
| Adjusted EBITDA is management defined; no bridge to covenant EBITDA; no pro forma for Windsor and Grand Bazaar | Leverage and cover could differ | Ratios | Medium | Treat ratios as indicative |
| Guarantor names, restricted group and Special Improvement District Bond security not supplied | Structural subordination analysis | Structure | Medium | Obtain guarantor exhibit and indentures |
| Withdrawal liability for multi-employer pension plans not found | Possible unrecorded claim | Claims outside debt | Low | Request disclosure |
| No external ratings, market prices or peer data; no outside material used | Not required for this scope | Relative value (not in scope) | Low | None |
## Next module

- CP-5: trace each CP-2 figure to its CP-1 figure or page locator; mark the ratios in the Calculations section as calculated (1.38x, 47.5%, 58, 59.1%); confirm the lease schedule figures against 10-K page:117; check the stated sign and direction of every comparison.

- Downstream use: carry the unresolved change of control, the missing covenant ratios and the 6.95x and 1.69x lease-inclusive measures as restrictions; do not treat the debt-only 3.26x as the whole leverage picture.

## Calculations
All inputs in USD millions from the cited pages or from CP-1 and CP-2. Every upstream derived number was recomputed; the results are in T5B.5. New calculations made in this audit:

- Lease-inclusive ratio at constant FY2025 EBITDA: 24,847 / 3,624 = 6.86x. Reported ratios: 25,001 / 3,624 = 6.90x and 24,847 / 3,573 = 6.95x. The change comes from the denominator: 3,573 - 3,624 = -51.

- Balance sheet carrying value of debt, September 30, 2026: 114 + 11,444 = 11,558; face 11,659 - 11,558 = 101 (unamortised discounts and deferred finance charges, 101 on the debt note). Leverage on carrying value: 11,558 / 3,573 = 3.23x. Net of cash 864: (11,558 - 864) / 3,573 = 2.99x. Lease-inclusive on carrying value: (11,558 + 13,188) / 3,573 = 6.93x.
- Liquidity availability net of letters of credit only: 2,250 + 25 - 96 = 2,179 at Q3 2026, against 2,083 on the company basis.

- Confidence score: lineage of the five material drivers: 2 Directly Sourced (weight 1.0), 2 Calculated (0.9), 1 Insufficient Information (0.0), E = (2 x 1.0 + 2 x 0.9 + 0) / 5 x 100 = 76.
